subject: Clarify billing on min-charge & context spillover
messages:
From: Maggie Li <maggie@bluepass.io>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: Bluepass Procurement <sourcing@bluepass.io>
Date: Tue, 23 May 2028 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify billing on min-charge & context spillover

Hi Sergio / Redwood finance team,

We're reviewing our June invoice and I need help understanding two items that materially change our effective price compared to the run-rate we expected:

1) Minimum charge "quantum" aggregation: multiple small calls on 6/11 and 6/12 were each rounded up to a full billing quantum. On the invoice it looks like three 120-token calls turned into 3x the min unit rather than being aggregated into one unit. Can you confirm the aggregation rule?

2) Context spillover: a few longer conversational sessions spilled into a second context window; we were expecting prefix aggregation to avoid double-charging for KV reuse. The invoice line shows separate charges for the two windows. Any explanation of how the context-length thresholds were applied would be helpful.

Attached a redacted invoice extract (Bluepass_June_invoice_sample.pdf) and the call log we exported (call_logs_202805.csv). Happy to hop on a short call if easier. We have a renewal conversation next week; if these are expected behavior we need to account for it in the final concession.

Thanks,
Maggie Li
Head of Platform Integrations
Bluepass Logistics

Attachments: Bluepass_June_invoice_sample.pdf (pdf), call_logs_202805.csv (csv)

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Maggie Li <maggie@bluepass.io>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, Bluepass Procurement <sourcing@bluepass.io>
Date: Tue, 23 May 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify billing on min-charge & context spillover

On Tue, May 23, 2028 at 9:17 AM Maggie Li <maggie@bluepass.io> wrote:
> We're reviewing our June invoice and I need help understanding two items that materially change our effective price compared to the run-rate we expected:
>
> 1) Minimum charge "quantum" aggregation...
> 2) Context spillover...

Hi Maggie — thanks for the clear examples and the attachments. Short answers first:

- Aggregation: by default we aggregate calls by conversation prefix and by a 10-minute activity window. However, our billing quantum is applied per-charge-window after aggregation; if calls are separated by long idle gaps or by different conversation IDs they do not coalesce.

- Context spillover: we bill additional context windows when the call's token footprint exceeds the model's single-window capacity. Prefix/KV reuse reduces token computation but doesn't avoid an additional window charge if the total input+context forces an overflow into a second context slab.

That said, I don't think the behavior you see should have produced three full min-unit charges for what looks like closely spaced 120-token calls. Can you confirm whether those three rows in the exported call log share the same conversation ID and were within a 10-minute window? If so, we should be able to collapse them and issue a credit.

Next steps I propose:
- Vanessa and Tessa: can you run the invoice->calllog reconciliation for Bluepass and produce a line-by-line delta? I started a quick calc and attached a draft concession (concession_draft.docx) with a proposed one-time credit to smooth the June overcharge.
- Maggie: if you can highlight the three call IDs you reference in the call_logs CSV that will speed things up.

I can jump on a 20-min call today if helpful.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: concession_draft.docx (docx)

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 24 May 2028 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Bluepass June invoice - reconciliation ask (BP-7632)

Team — internal note (please do not forward raw):

I pulled the sample and started mapping invoice lines to call logs. Preliminary findings:
- The invoice shows three "min-quantum" hits on 2028-06-11. The three UUIDs (call_aa1, call_bb2, call_cc3) share the same conversation_id but have gaps of ~14 and ~9 minutes between them. Our current window is 10 minutes, so the first gap breaks aggregation and explains separate quantums.
- The longer session on 6/12 spilled into a second context slab because their prompt+history hit ~33k tokens and our 32k slab threshold was exceeded. KV reuse reduced compute inside each slab but could not avoid the slab boundary charge.

Options for customer-facing resolution:
1) Technical explanation + one-time smoothing credit for June (covers the two extra min-quanta) — simple and keeps renewal on track.
2) Offer to lower their aggregation idle window to 15 minutes for this account for 3 months (config opt-in) so similar patterns won't reoccur — this requires product signoff but is doable as an account-level override.
3) Contract amendment to clarify slab behavior and include a Cap(%) on per-invoice quantum uplift for the next 6 months.

Recommend option 1 + offer option 2 as a goodwill pilot. Vanessa, draft the credit amount and legal language; Tessa, what's the lift to enable a 15-min aggregation override in config?

Sergio

From: Maggie Li <maggie@bluepass.io>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: Bluepass Procurement <sourcing@bluepass.io>, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 25 May 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify billing on min-charge & context spillover

Thanks — that explanation helps and matches our export once I filter by conversation_id. We'd like to take option 1 (one-time smoothing credit) and also pilot the 15-minute aggregation window for the next quarter. Two small asks to finalize:

- Please send a short concession letter we can attach to procurement (PDF).
- Can you confirm the credit amount and whether the pilot requires a change in the contract (we prefer an account-level opt-in that doesn't change master terms).

If you can get the concession letter and a HubSpot note (link to deal included above) by end of day tomorrow we'll route internally and aim to sign before renewal.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Maggie

Attachments referenced earlier: Bluepass_June_invoice_sample.pdf, call_logs_202805.csv
